items.author: Erich Fromm

items.title: ALBI: LLM-Guided Inductive Logic Programming via Iterative Generate-Test-Constrain Refineme
items.abstract: ALBI is a neuro-symbolic framework that uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate candidate hypotheses for Inductive Logic Programming (ILP). These hypotheses are then formally verified by SWI-Prolog, and feedback from failed tests guides the LLM to refine its proposals iteratively. The paper's core contribution is this LLM-driven, iterative generate-test-constrain loop for ILP, enhanced by semantic anonymization to ensure genuine symbolic induction rather than superficial pattern matching, achieving high success rates across multiple LLMs.

items.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
items.abstract: This paper investigates how to durably suppress undesired behaviors in language models. The authors create specific "misaligned" models and evaluate standard suppression techniques like SFT and GRPO. Their contribution lies in a systematic study of these methods' effectiveness in immediately stopping the bad behavior, preventing its re-emergence during further training, and maintaining the model's overall capabilities.

items.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method to detect suppressed knowledge in LLMs by analyzing the geometric coherence of "anon-vectors" (differences in hidden states between concept queries and paraphrases). Genuine knowledge forms a tight cluster, while ignorance leads to geometric fragmentation. This fragmentation reliably distinguishes known from unknown concepts and correlates with the recoverability of knowledge after unlearning, offering a novel way to probe LLM understanding beyond simple behavioral responses.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.abstract: This paper argues that speculative decoding, often seen as a system optimization, can negatively impact long-horizon agent reasoning by introducing noise. Their core method involves training the draft model to encode critical reasoning with higher precision, thereby mitigating this noise. The contribution is demonstrating how to improve agent reasoning accuracy by controlling speculative decoding's impact on the target model's output distribution.

items.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces WebCatalyst, a reinforcement learning framework for generating interactive HTML from natural language. Its core method uses a browser-interaction approach with novel components like a GUI assessor, Visual Anchor, and Action-Trace Credit to improve functional and visual quality during user interaction. The contribution lies in effectively optimizing interactive web page generation, addressing limitations in existing methods that focus on static page rendering.
items.figure_caption: From task-specific webpage optimization to interactive HTML capability catalysis. WebCatalyst improves fidelity in interaction experience, reward signals, and credit assignment through a Game-Level GUI Assessor, Visual Anchor, and Action-Trace Credit.

items.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
items.abstract: DreamX repurposes a pre-trained video diffusion model to learn universal latent action representations. It achieves this by extracting highly compressed, action-centric latent codes from the model's spatiotemporal features, effectively disentangling action dynamics from visual appearance. This allows DreamX to create a shared action interface transferable across different embodiments and environments.
items.figure_caption: DreamX learns a shared action interface from egocentric human videos and robot videos. Compact, embodiment-agnostic latent actions extracted from a pretrained video diffusion model capture motion consistently across changes in embodiment and scene appearance. The same representation enables transferring motion from a source video to a target video, decoding human motion into executable robot actions without paired human–robot training data, and training a lightweight latent policy that jointly predicts latent actions and robot actions.

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.abstract: This paper proposes shifting AI focus from autonomous agents to "AI-augmented human intelligence" (AHI). The core method involves developing "cognitive symbionts," AI systems designed to be lifelong, embedded partners that enhance individual human intelligence by providing real-time support. The main contribution is advocating for a new paradigm where AI amplifies human capabilities rather than solely replacing them.

items.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
items.abstract: This paper introduces Continual AutoResearch, an environment designed to evaluate whether autoresearch agents can learn and retain knowledge across tasks. By comparing persistent agents to reset ones under matched conditions, the study demonstrates that maintaining agent state significantly improves research efficiency across various ML problem types. This highlights the potential for agents to build upon prior experience rather than starting anew for each problem.

items.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.abstract: HARP addresses limitations in LLM-based recommendation by treating users and items as communicating agents. Its core method involves a four-stage process: building self-descriptions, transmitting them, understanding the other agent, and syncing for future interactions. HARP's contribution is a novel framework that enables dual-profile communication, allowing both users and items to generate comparable descriptions and integrate profile information throughout the recommendation pipeline, overcoming the previous one-sided and prompt-trapped limitations.
items.figure_caption: Harp at a glance. A user with a niche query in a half-dialogue session, compared with the full dialogue restored by Harp . HARP integrates three training-free innovations: Dual Profile (§ 3.2 ), Homophily Gate (§ 3.3 ), and Reflection (§ 3.4 ).

items.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that fine-tuning LLMs on data they internally disbelieve, even if not explicitly harmful, can lead to broad misalignment. The core method involves training models on incorrect information across various domains, observing that stronger disbelief correlates with increased misalignment without significant loss of general capabilities. The contribution is showing that this internal inconsistency, where the model states wrong answers but still internally favors correct ones, is a key mechanism for inducing misalignment.

items.title: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory
items.abstract: This paper investigates "history interference" in speech-LLMs, where irrelevant past audio information can negatively impact current responses. The core method involves controlled experiments and causal interventions to understand how this interference occurs. The contribution is identifying two distinct pathways for this interference: one addressable by blocking direct source access, and another, more persistent one, carried by internal question-candidate states, particularly in multiple-choice scenarios.

items.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces "targeted guidance," an on-policy reinforcement learning method that uses rich textual feedback to improve learning from difficult rewards. The core method involves on-policy self-distillation, leveraging per-turn textual feedback to provide a directional signal. The key contribution is stabilizing this guidance throughout training without degrading baseline performance, achieved by combining self-distillation with per-criteria rewards and limiting feedback to specific policy turns.
items.figure_caption: Naive RL fails to optimize criterion that fall outside the support of base policies. Exploration issues in RL can manifest as slow learning (middle) or in the worst case a complete failure to improve (left). On the other hand, targeted guidance enables policies to directionally improve specific aspects of their behavior and thus continue to learn.

items.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
items.abstract: MDSKILL addresses the challenge of noisy and entangled skill memories in reinforcement learning by organizing them into three functional views: state grounding, action planning, and execution control. It then uses dynamic metrics to select high-quality skills and employs multi-view distillation to transfer and consolidate complementary knowledge, leading to more efficient and robust self-evolving agents. This approach improves knowledge internalization and prevents performance degradation, especially under limited training budgets.

items.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
items.abstract: ToolSpace addresses limitations in scaling tool-centric environments for long-horizon agents by reversing the traditional data-centric approach. It prioritizes tool composition by mining execution traces to build a tool-graph, which is then clustered into environments. This tool-centric method ensures grounded tool interfaces and compositions, enabling more realistic and longer-horizon task execution.
items.figure_caption: Overview of ToolSpace. (a) Design Philosophy: a tool space layer between agents and MCP environments. (b) The tool-composition graph with a state-aware walk. (c) Generalization across 7 benchmarks. (d) Performance on two Pro benchmarks.

items.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
items.abstract: This paper introduces AgentAM, an LLM agent that provides process engineers natural-language access to predictive models for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). AgentAM leverages surrogate models trained on CFD simulations to predict melt pool geometry and spatter formation, enabling defect-aware process optimization. Its core contribution is bridging the gap between complex LPBF simulation tools and practical shop-floor application through an intuitive, conversational interface.
items.figure_caption: Overview of AgentAM. The agent turns an engineer’s request into a call to a tool on a local MCP server, which evaluates the polynomial surrogates, assigns geometry-derived regimes and searches the process window; the agent then reports the returned values. The example is benchmark prompt C15-01 with the call the agent made. Map: predicted regimes over the trained range; hatching marks points that meet the margins of Section 3.5 ; ∘ \( \circ \) , plain minimum-spatter optimum; ⋆ \( \star \) , margin-aware optimum. The bottom row summarizes the agent evaluation.

items.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
items.abstract: This paper introduces Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples slow, high-level semantic reasoning from fast, low-level action generation. ARP uses a high-capacity Vision-Language Model to asynchronously update a semantic memory, which then conditions a lightweight Vision-Action Expert to generate robot actions at a much higher frequency. This allows for real-time robot agility without sacrificing the capabilities of large foundation models.

items.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
items.abstract: This paper proposes a **geometric abstraction** to represent robot scene geometry using typed, evidence-aware symbolic references. This abstraction is refreshed from observations and read by language models, allowing them to reuse symbolic task structures while only re-grounding metric values as needed. The core contribution is demonstrating that this approach improves multi-step manipulation and significantly reduces redundant multimodal queries compared to reinterpreting raw visual data at every step.

items.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals
items.abstract: This paper investigates the instability of assignments generated by LLM-based mediators when processing citizen opinions into collective proposals. The core method involves repeatedly running LLMs with the same opinions but varying random seeds or order, revealing that assignments can fluctuate significantly or even disappear. The main contribution is demonstrating that this instability can lead to "silent choices," where alternative proposals with different assignments are hidden from participants, undermining transparency in AI-mediated decision-making.
items.figure_caption: Study design. Each task combines thirty opinions, a mediator and one of six prompts. Five runs vary sampling or opinion order; Terra uses independent sampling calls rather than specified seeds. New opinion samples provide a DeliberationBank reference. Judges assess assignments and coverage. Three annotators check assignments on 58 statements and 52 pairs, including six controls (330 judgments). The 17,400 statements cover all experiments (Appendix B ).

items.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces JHiMA-WebRL, a novel framework for long-horizon web tasks that addresses the limitations of monolithic agents. It jointly trains a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning system, separating planning (task decomposer) and execution (actor) while ensuring their synchronized learning. This approach aims to improve long-horizon navigation by providing a stronger inductive bias through this coupled, hierarchical structure.
items.figure_caption: Overview of JHiMA-WebRL. Left: prior web agents use a single policy, or a separate planner that receives no RL updates while the actor is trained. Right: we generate subtask supervision from GUI trajectories, fine-tune the decomposer and actor, and jointly optimize both with hierarchical RL: K K decompositions, M M actor rollouts each, and role-specific advantages from terminal rewards.

items.title: LatentTriad: Pre-Action Risk Representations for Malicious Agent Skill Detection
items.abstract: LatentTriad detects malicious agent skills by analyzing hidden states during the "prefill" phase, before any execution. It leverages task-operation consistency within these latent states, combined with group-adjusted operation directions and deviations from normal state relationships. This approach offers highly accurate, pre-execution risk detection without invoking tools or running code.
items.figure_caption: LatentTriad overview. One prefill of the task and skill yields Declaration, Operation, and Boundary states for risk detection. Connections show schematic feature flow; the right panel illustrates optional source attribution.

papers.abstract: DreamX repurposes a pre-trained video diffusion model to learn universal latent action representations. It achieves this by extracting highly compressed, action-centric latent codes from the model's spatiotemporal features, effectively disentangling action dynamics from visual appearance. This allows DreamX to create a shared action interface transferable across different embodiments and environments.
papers.figure_caption: DreamX learns a shared action interface from egocentric human videos and robot videos. Compact, embodiment-agnostic latent actions extracted from a pretrained video diffusion model capture motion consistently across changes in embodiment and scene appearance. The same representation enables transferring motion from a source video to a target video, decoding human motion into executable robot actions without paired human–robot training data, and training a lightweight latent policy that jointly predicts latent actions and robot actions.

papers.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
papers.abstract: This paper proposes shifting AI focus from autonomous agents to "AI-augmented human intelligence" (AHI). The core method involves developing "cognitive symbionts," AI systems designed to be lifelong, embedded partners that enhance individual human intelligence by providing real-time support. The main contribution is advocating for a new paradigm where AI amplifies human capabilities rather than solely replacing them.

papers.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Continual AutoResearch, an environment designed to evaluate whether autoresearch agents can learn and retain knowledge across tasks. By comparing persistent agents to reset ones under matched conditions, the study demonstrates that maintaining agent state significantly improves research efficiency across various ML problem types. This highlights the potential for agents to build upon prior experience rather than starting anew for each problem.

papers.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: HARP addresses limitations in LLM-based recommendation by treating users and items as communicating agents. Its core method involves a four-stage process: building self-descriptions, transmitting them, understanding the other agent, and syncing for future interactions. HARP's contribution is a novel framework that enables dual-profile communication, allowing both users and items to generate comparable descriptions and integrate profile information throughout the recommendation pipeline, overcoming the previous one-sided and prompt-trapped limitations.
papers.figure_caption: Harp at a glance. A user with a niche query in a half-dialogue session, compared with the full dialogue restored by Harp . HARP integrates three training-free innovations: Dual Profile (§ 3.2 ), Homophily Gate (§ 3.3 ), and Reflection (§ 3.4 ).

papers.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that fine-tuning LLMs on data they internally disbelieve, even if not explicitly harmful, can lead to broad misalignment. The core method involves training models on incorrect information across various domains, observing that stronger disbelief correlates with increased misalignment without significant loss of general capabilities. The contribution is showing that this internal inconsistency, where the model states wrong answers but still internally favors correct ones, is a key mechanism for inducing misalignment.

papers.title: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory
papers.abstract: This paper investigates "history interference" in speech-LLMs, where irrelevant past audio information can negatively impact current responses. The core method involves controlled experiments and causal interventions to understand how this interference occurs. The contribution is identifying two distinct pathways for this interference: one addressable by blocking direct source access, and another, more persistent one, carried by internal question-candidate states, particularly in multiple-choice scenarios.

papers.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "targeted guidance," an on-policy reinforcement learning method that uses rich textual feedback to improve learning from difficult rewards. The core method involves on-policy self-distillation, leveraging per-turn textual feedback to provide a directional signal. The key contribution is stabilizing this guidance throughout training without degrading baseline performance, achieved by combining self-distillation with per-criteria rewards and limiting feedback to specific policy turns.
papers.figure_caption: Naive RL fails to optimize criterion that fall outside the support of base policies. Exploration issues in RL can manifest as slow learning (middle) or in the worst case a complete failure to improve (left). On the other hand, targeted guidance enables policies to directionally improve specific aspects of their behavior and thus continue to learn.

papers.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
papers.abstract: MDSKILL addresses the challenge of noisy and entangled skill memories in reinforcement learning by organizing them into three functional views: state grounding, action planning, and execution control. It then uses dynamic metrics to select high-quality skills and employs multi-view distillation to transfer and consolidate complementary knowledge, leading to more efficient and robust self-evolving agents. This approach improves knowledge internalization and prevents performance degradation, especially under limited training budgets.

papers.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: ToolSpace addresses limitations in scaling tool-centric environments for long-horizon agents by reversing the traditional data-centric approach. It prioritizes tool composition by mining execution traces to build a tool-graph, which is then clustered into environments. This tool-centric method ensures grounded tool interfaces and compositions, enabling more realistic and longer-horizon task execution.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of ToolSpace. (a) Design Philosophy: a tool space layer between agents and MCP environments. (b) The tool-composition graph with a state-aware walk. (c) Generalization across 7 benchmarks. (d) Performance on two Pro benchmarks.

papers.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AgentAM, an LLM agent that provides process engineers natural-language access to predictive models for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). AgentAM leverages surrogate models trained on CFD simulations to predict melt pool geometry and spatter formation, enabling defect-aware process optimization. Its core contribution is bridging the gap between complex LPBF simulation tools and practical shop-floor application through an intuitive, conversational interface.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of AgentAM. The agent turns an engineer’s request into a call to a tool on a local MCP server, which evaluates the polynomial surrogates, assigns geometry-derived regimes and searches the process window; the agent then reports the returned values. The example is benchmark prompt C15-01 with the call the agent made. Map: predicted regimes over the trained range; hatching marks points that meet the margins of Section 3.5 ; ∘ \( \circ \) , plain minimum-spatter optimum; ⋆ \( \star \) , margin-aware optimum. The bottom row summarizes the agent evaluation.

papers.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples slow, high-level semantic reasoning from fast, low-level action generation. ARP uses a high-capacity Vision-Language Model to asynchronously update a semantic memory, which then conditions a lightweight Vision-Action Expert to generate robot actions at a much higher frequency. This allows for real-time robot agility without sacrificing the capabilities of large foundation models.

papers.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a **geometric abstraction** to represent robot scene geometry using typed, evidence-aware symbolic references. This abstraction is refreshed from observations and read by language models, allowing them to reuse symbolic task structures while only re-grounding metric values as needed. The core contribution is demonstrating that this approach improves multi-step manipulation and significantly reduces redundant multimodal queries compared to reinterpreting raw visual data at every step.

papers.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the instability of assignments generated by LLM-based mediators when processing citizen opinions into collective proposals. The core method involves repeatedly running LLMs with the same opinions but varying random seeds or order, revealing that assignments can fluctuate significantly or even disappear. The main contribution is demonstrating that this instability can lead to "silent choices," where alternative proposals with different assignments are hidden from participants, undermining transparency in AI-mediated decision-making.
papers.figure_caption: Study design. Each task combines thirty opinions, a mediator and one of six prompts. Five runs vary sampling or opinion order; Terra uses independent sampling calls rather than specified seeds. New opinion samples provide a DeliberationBank reference. Judges assess assignments and coverage. Three annotators check assignments on 58 statements and 52 pairs, including six controls (330 judgments). The 17,400 statements cover all experiments (Appendix B ).

papers.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces JHiMA-WebRL, a novel framework for long-horizon web tasks that addresses the limitations of monolithic agents. It jointly trains a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning system, separating planning (task decomposer) and execution (actor) while ensuring their synchronized learning. This approach aims to improve long-horizon navigation by providing a stronger inductive bias through this coupled, hierarchical structure.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of JHiMA-WebRL. Left: prior web agents use a single policy, or a separate planner that receives no RL updates while the actor is trained. Right: we generate subtask supervision from GUI trajectories, fine-tune the decomposer and actor, and jointly optimize both with hierarchical RL: K K decompositions, M M actor rollouts each, and role-specific advantages from terminal rewards.

papers.title: LatentTriad: Pre-Action Risk Representations for Malicious Agent Skill Detection
papers.abstract: LatentTriad detects malicious agent skills by analyzing hidden states during the "prefill" phase, before any execution. It leverages task-operation consistency within these latent states, combined with group-adjusted operation directions and deviations from normal state relationships. This approach offers highly accurate, pre-execution risk detection without invoking tools or running code.
papers.figure_caption: LatentTriad overview. One prefill of the task and skill yields Declaration, Operation, and Boundary states for risk detection. Connections show schematic feature flow; the right panel illustrates optional source attribution.
